card.name: Word starts after a break in drug text
card.fires_on: The word or letter that begins a new clause or term in drug-label text, often a lone capital letter or first letter such as H, T or t. It also fires on small words like for or avoid before a verb phrase.

modes.label: Lone first letter
modes.description: A single letter that starts a longer medical word, which is finished by the next piece of text.
modes.example: The effects of<< h>>emo- or peritoneal dialysis

modes.label: Start of new sentence or heading
modes.description: A capital letter that opens a new sentence or an all-caps heading right after a period.
modes.example: lethal levels can be reached in a few hours.<< T>>REATMENT OF HYPERKALEM

modes.label: Linking word before a purpose phrase
modes.description: A small word such as for or avoid that leads into a purpose or action phrase.
modes.example: To<< avoid>> distress to the patient, do not administer

card.plain: It marks the first letter of a medical word or sentence in a drug label, when the rest of the word is still to come.
